match.reason: The closest bank point, bio-meiosis, covers all of meiosis and only touches crossing over and independent assortment as two of its four bullets, so it is broader than this focused point and is written for a Year 12 NSW course rather than VCE Year 11.

draft.title: Crossing over and independent assortment
card: in prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair up and swap matching sections. This makes new combinations of alleles on the same chromosome.
in metaphase I, each homologous pair lines up at the cell's centre in a random way. Which chromosome of a pair goes to which side does not depend on how any other pair lines up.
A human cell has 23 pairs, so independent assortment alone can make 2^23 (over 8 million) combinations of chromosomes in a gamete.
Both processes happen during meiosis. Together they mean the gametes from one person carry different mixes of alleles, which adds to variation in offspring.
draft.remember: Crossing over mixes alleles within a chromosome. Independent assortment mixes whole chromosomes between gametes.

a.q: Which event in meiosis creates a chromosome with a new combination of alleles along its length?
opts: Swapping of sections between homologous chromosomes
Random lining-up of homologous pairs at the centre
Halving of the chromosome number in each gamete
Copying of DNA before the cell begins to divide
a.why: Swapping sections between homologous chromosomes (crossing over) puts alleles from one chromosome onto the other, so each chromosome carries a new mix. Random lining-up moves whole chromosomes into different gametes, but it does not change the alleles along a single chromosome.
a.clue: Think about which event changes a chromosome itself, not just where it ends up.

b.q: Kiri's cells have 3 homologous pairs of chromosomes. Ignoring crossing over, how many different combinations of chromosomes can her gametes have?
b.why: Each pair lines up independently and can go either way, so the number of combinations is 2 × 2 × 2 = 2^3 = 8. Six is a tempting answer from adding 2 + 2 + 2, but the pairs combine by multiplying because each choice is independent.
b.clue: Each pair has two ways to line up, and the pairs do not affect each other.

a.best: Swapping of sections between homologous chromosomes
